comment: Great hike. I'm glad we brought out dog backpack for our small dog. Some steep sections. Parking lot is right at nice beach. If we knew we would have brought swim suits for after the hike.
Some challenging inclines with a rewarding lookout view. BTW F*CK PARKINSON'S
Must do trail!! Hard but worth it.
Lots of mosquitos

It rained lightly the entire hike. The trail is excellent - well marked and folks have made casual trails up and around particularly muddy spots and sections of trail that traverse exposed rock. The rain made the bugs a non-factor for the most part. The view at the top was shrouded in clouds, but still lovely. Oddly , the rain stopped just as my hike ended.
Downed tree
bugs

Got to the trail by 9am to try and beat the heat. A lot of mosquitos at the start but got better as we got higher up. Definitely some muddy spots but manageable with hiking boots. The top view is breathtaking and the second half of the hike is much easier going downhill and not as deep in the forest, going along the water. Definitely recommend doing the trail clockwise, so you are not having to go up many stairs.
Great view. Vicious flys.

Overall a quick and well marked trail, good views from after the climb. Partly muddy and bugs. Second half of the trail (if doing clockwise) is way better, lot of stairs to make the climb down easier.

The rail bed is hard to notice, I didn’t see it but I think we walked on it and it was grown over? ANYWAY the cliff and its view more than make up for it. It was incredible and so cool to be on top of a drop. We went after it had rained overnight so it was muddy, but it honestly wasn’t bad.

Some pretty muddy and buggy sections in the first third of the hike but otherwise a really great hike. The views from Booth's Rock might be the best in the park, in my opinion. The final stretch along the lakeshore is also quite scenic, and the beaver dam makes for lots of good bird and wildlife watching.

A bit muddy after rain but nothing too bad. A lot of bugs and mosquitoes this time of year especially in the first half of the trail. Didn’t see much at the ruins but still cool. Panoramic views are amazing!
Beautiful trail. Not really difficult. The views are worth the hike.
Beautiful spots! Wasn’t buggy in the morning taking the trail counterclockwise but became buggy at the end. Would recommend long pants and sleeves. Some inclines but pretty easy overall.
My husband and I and our dog Sophie we hiked the trail 👣 today! The bugs 🐛 were very bad today but we survived! The views at the lookouts are some of the most beautiful spots in Algonquin Park!
Appreciate the blue circles on trees making it simple to follow the trail
We love this trail. Huge payoff with gorgeous views of Rock Lake at the top (about halfway). The climb is worth the reward. And a nice set of stairs on the way down.
muddy, no bugs, lots of stairs and incline
Great views! The trail was not buggy at all. A few muddy spots but nothing bad.
Moderate trek
beautiful views and sick beaver dam

Trail was amazing!! A few things to note: 
1) the driving path to the trail head was closed for maintenance, you could still park at the main cabins but it added and extra 1.2KM walk to get to the beginning of the trail. 
2) the path is extremely well marked but it is very much the forest floor. Lots of big roots, rocks and up and downs. 
3) the large steep hill comes right after the portage area HOWEVER it is quite brief. After that it is very reasonably hilly. 
4) the large decline is actually stairs. So don’t let that discourage anyone with bad knee’s 
5) there wasn’t a single soul out there with us, we saw lot’s of cute wildlife and even the home of an otter!
still a beautiful hike on a cold rainy spring day. first section muddy with some ice. extra few km as rock lake camp still closed so have to park at main gate
Amazing views. One of my top 3 faves in the park.
Great view of the lake, even with it iced over
The last 1 km to the trailhead is closed to vehicles for the winter. There is parking at the comfort station.
One of the nicest in Algonquin

Great trail and wasn’t crowded to my surprise. The fall colours from the lookout are mostly out now, but it was still a beautiful view.

Most of the trail itself contains many evergreen trees, so the hike up was very beautiful and looked especially serene after rain in the morning.

Most of the hike is easy except a few areas with slight incline, which are still very doable.
Lovely trail! We missed the peak fall colors but the view from the top was still worth it!

Had a fun time with this hike! Colours have definitely faded and most leaves have fallen apart from the pine trees. Great weather this Sunday mostly overcast, no bugs and only passed by 3 groups. Note that we are fit and able bodied so we pretty much flew through the trail and we wanted to beat the times AllTrails and the Visitors Centre approximated (2-2.5h). Walked over rocks, gravel, board walk, and lots of leaves (slippery due to previous rainfall). Lots of view points the first isn’t the best, keep going! 
- Allayna & Hafsa
Stunning views! Slippery due to leaves, so just be cautious. It does go right along the cliff for a short while. Absolutely gorgeous!

Beautiful trail, slight incline to get to lookout but manageable. The descent and return is mostly on stairs and along flat road
Great lookout
Great hike to experience the area. Colorful trees mostly down
Nice views

It was a great trail, insane views. Not too crazy busy. Parking lot is smaller...so arrive early if you think it's going to be busy...or you'll have quite the hike from the entrance of the campground to the hike itself.

Great 5km circuit hike with spectacular views, cool forest, wood stairs, and golden sand beach near the end.  Quite crowded however at top of bluff (50 people all standing around), otherwise a 5 star hike!

Excellent hike to some beautiful views of the trees and lake. Wonderful rocks! Many picture opportunities. Very well marked, but can be very busy during the autumn peak colours. Camping at Rock Lake you can walk to trail head.
Amazing colours and views from the top. I would skip the estate part though.
Hiked 26-Sept-2025. Great colours and weather. Minimal crowds if you start at first light around 7 am!
One of the best hikes in the area for sure. Breathtaking views, variety of environments, plus well marked and maintained trails. Challenging, but not impossible. Worth making time for!
Great hike to the top of a cliff, with great views.
Take side trails for added interest.

I was on my honeymoon and had the flu…bad timing.  We still went to the park and Booth’s Rock wasn’t too difficult for me - a 46 year old man who is somewhat active and was sick at the time haha!  

The trails were clear and mostly easy to navigate.  Going up was the most work but very fun.  The views from the cliffs were unreal.  Definitely the best part of the trail.   Getting back down was not bad.  They have wooden stairs to help get you down the steepest parts.  Much appreciated by us.   

We did the trail in about 1 hour and 50 minutes, which included stopping at the top for about ten minutes.  I highly recommend this one.
Fall foliage was at peak.
Beautiful scenic views
There are always great views, particularly in the Fall.
Beautiful hike that offers beautiful views, small bursts of uphill climbs, and overall a very worthwhile trail to visit while at Algonquin!
Really nice trail. Lots of character, great views, well marked and easy to follow. Wasn't too busy but with colour change starting there was a constant flow of people.
Bring poles
Views are breathtaking. Trees are just starting to show their colours.
Bit of a climb, and lots of steps back down. But great views from the top. Very clear trail.
Incredible views, fund exploring where the estate used to be, and terrain makes it difficult but fun!
Well marked, stunning views
Loved the view about half way through the hike. Reasonably easy with an 8 year old. Good variety of nature to take in. Beaver dams near the end were cool to see.
Beautiful trail through the forest, then an abandoned railroad bed at the end. Views from the lookout ridge are stunning!
Fun hike! Lots of great views. The third lookout spot was our favorite. No cell reception for most of the trail.

We walked to the trail head from Rock Pond campground A which added another mile making it a 5 or so mile hike. Definitely on the easier side. Cliff rocks provided a great view and much better cell service.  The side trail to the house was waste - house long gone.
A very nice hike!  Great views.  When you think you’ve hit the overlook, go a little farther, it opens up even more.
Nice trail.  It would be gorgeous in the fall with the changing leaves.
Well maintained, great views. I just didn’t like the last km that wasn’t in the forest.

My perfect day hike! You could probably do the loop in just over an hour, but you will want to take your time to enjoy the amazing views. Up- and downhill throughout so it didn’t feel like such a steep climb until you get to the lookouts on top, lots of variety in the terrain and not too busy even on a summer Saturday. Gorgeous lake too!

The views are beautiful but the walk is unusual. Cars be wary because the roads are scary. The prices are high and there are many flies. Be prepared because unlike us you won’t be scared. Overall it’s a W trail, and we recommend it so don’t fail.
Great lookout. The railbed was pretty cool through the rocks. My 5 year old did this hike no problem.

Try to mmm
Nh by
Great trail, well marked. Amazing vistas
Great well marked trail with incredible views! Had lunch at the top - simply gorgeous!

Excellent Trail with viewpoints after the small climb and views of the lake below with a massive cliff drop. Easy, nice climb down to the parking area which is next to the entrance and start of the walk. I highly recommend it.

Do the trail in the recommend order. Don't listen to anyone who wants you to climb a thousand stairs rather than go down them LOL. I don't agree that this has the best lookouts in the 60 area (that's Centennial Ridges) nor that it's the best trail (that's track and tower) but this is like a mini ridges. An argument can be made for fall on this trail, but it's easier to get tailor swift tickets than to get a fall parking pass here.
Great trail, very few bugs, nice views along the trail. Probably on the low end of moderate difficulty.
Enjoyed this short little evening  hike. Views are amazing and well worth it. Staircase coming down was incredible.  Not too many bugs.
The best view among the trails off Hwy 60 in Algonquin. Today was a pleasant 23C after a long heat wave with little mud and few bugs.

Great trail with some challenging parts. The tall cliffs offer beautiful views of the surrounding area! Strongly recommend to do this trail in the proposed direction (entrance towards the left at the end of the parking lot). Can easily be accessed from the Rock Lake campground, especially the B section. Do not miss!
Great view point moderate 5km hike
It’s a trail with astonishing views. The first portion has muddy areas which are easily navigable if you have walking poles.

Some things to know. It's a beautiful lake and fantastic trail, but more than moderate, esp the first 2/3 which are steep and muddy. Took us twice as long as All Trails predicted. Consider just going in reverse to see the ruined mansion and swim or fish on that side of the lake. If you do go in order, be sure to pick up the paper guide at the trail head, which has I teresting info about the history of the land along the trail.
My husband and I and our dog sophie we hiked the trail  today! We have hiked the this trail quite a few times! It is a moderate trail beautiful views!
Hard trail if it’s not something you do every other day :) but it’s doable ! There was muddy spots
Great views at the top and a very enjoyable and well laid out trail. 5mile sand road drive from Highway 60.
Great views, excellent trail. A little muddy in spots but usually easy workarounds. Enjoy!
nice hike. great views from lookouts.   a little muddy following thunderstorm the day prior.  some mosquitos in darker areas of forest.  easy parking.

Muddy, buggy but fun trail. The last part of the trail is on gravel so not the best for the dog, especially if it’s super hot like it was for us. Awesome but very tiny dog beach after the gravel so we can rinse some of the mud!
Parking tend to be full at morning. Muddy at places, but walk able. Views are great .
Muddy when there has been recent rain. Wear waterproof hiking shoes.
Definitely bring waterproof shoes, very wet in the lower spots. Saw 2 moose!
Amazing
Excellent hike!  Nice views.   Uphill climb was strenuous at times.  Downhill after booths rock .
Great hike, little muddy but overall was a success! Recommend eating lunch at the lookout (as long as it’s not too busy) 10/10
A little boggy at parts. Steep climbs. Great views. Lots of stairs to go down.
Very muddy at some parts, great view at the top.
A little muddy but all passable. Great views, great trail.
Downed trees in many spots on the trail. Nothing was impassable, but hopefully that all gets cleared soon. A bit mucky following ~15mm of rain yesterday, but as always, a beautiful trail.
Amazing trail to do for Mother’s Day solo !
Nice gentle climb and then beautiful views over Rock Lake
Snowshoes is a must and prepare for a long walk to the trail head as they don’t plow the road up to the trail head
Beautiful snowy day… did mostly in snowshoes. Wasn’t 100% necessary, but was glad I had them

Great hike that gives epic views and moderate difficulty terrain depending on time of year! Today was moody, misty rainy. Lots of mud, slippery leaves but still a favourite of mine! Poles recommended, unfortunately lots of garbage left behind. Picked up as much as I could in my pack.
Beautiful viewpoints! I’m mid-November you might still encounter some muddy patches, yet absolutely worth it!
All trails stopping working, did complete the full hike. Amazing day even though gloomy and moody rains came. Muddy, rocky, rooted terrain. High cliffs. Uses caution. Pick up your garbage!

Standalone permit required during peak season. I went in Nov and only regular Algonquin hwy60 permit is needed. 
Trail can be challenging with lots of ups and downs. It gets really muddy after rain. 
The view on top is exceptional and definitely worth the workout. 
Would recommend 100%.
trail is in great condition, leaves are gone therefore so are the crowds, i was the only one on the trail. great views. took me an hour to complete
Best trail I saw in the whole park. Great views and cool staircase.
Couldn’t of picked a better day for it. A little mud here or there but skip able. Definitely one of the better hikes in Algonquin
A big FO to all the people who leave toilet paper along this otherwise perfect trail.
Cliffs are 100% amazing
Love nature
A bit crowded on long weekend Sunday.
An easy trail, the vistas are magnificent!
Great views, not too busy on  Friday at 8 am. Very busy on the weekend.

We were super excited to finally cross this off our list. Currently the park is requiring a separate pass to access this trail due to the limited parking, plan accordingly. The trail was ideal for us, front end is a gorgeous walk through a pine forest leading to the summit. In our opinion the summit is the nicest lookout in the park. Fall colours are perfect, and we only encountered a couple of wet spots.  We were first on the trail and didn’t see a soul.
Muddy
The best trail in Algonquin park imo. Great views and variety throughout the trail.
Stunning! Had to walk from canoe launch,  bc so busy.  A vut crowded but seen worse. We were a group of 4,  60÷. Took it nice and easy. Beautiful day, beautiful scenery.
Great trail with spectacular views. Highly recommended

The fall views are STUNNING from the look-out. As beginners we find the trail itself quite challenging for beginners. It took us 3.5 hours to finish the trail. It has a few steep slopes, and we stopped to find directions twice. There are also a lot of muddy spots, but I guess it’s like this all-year-round. I like the humidity though. After all, the view is worth the walk!!

It was a bit muddy in spots, but otherwise it’s a lovely hike to see fall colours and views. A permit is required in the autumn because it’s a popular hike. Cell service is weak so buy it beforehand as you won’t be able to get it when you’re there.
Camped over, hit the trail at dawn. Could not have been more stunning.
The trail was very muddy in some sections. Would recommend either trail runners, low ankle boots, or trekking poles. Unbelievable fall colours.
such a good challenge!! beautiful views and a good workout
Need special Ontario Parks permit (Daily Vehicle Pass - Booth's Rock Trail + Hwy 60)

Amazing Panaromic views from the lookouts- Loved the varied terrain through out the hike. 
Heads-up: The parking spot has to be booked 5 days in advance & gets booked like crazy within few seconds after opening up. 
Highly recommend!

Wow, revisiting Booth’s Rock Trail after a few years and it’s just as awesome as we remembered. A great short distance with lots to look at and a gorgeous viewpoint. 
Currently it’s slightly muddy - wear hiking boots/waterproof shoes.
Abandoned railway track, and an amazing view point during fall times!
Overrated
Great day at Booth Rock trail
The views at the top are stunning.
Amazing views well worth the hike! Some steep hills and very rooty areas with some boardwalks and sections with stairs.
Great trail!
a short one. easy and leisure walk.
Fairly muddy
Loop closed at lookout point.
Closed untill September 6, 2024 for bridge reconstruction
Colorful mushrooms and lots of frogs. Trail was muddy and parts of it were closed due to construction but still a good hike got to see two good views of a lake

Lovely forest stroll with a great view! 

(Requires a pass from Ontario Provincial Parks to park at the trailhead.)

I dropped a red poncho on my way back down and didn’t notice until the next day, when I had left the area - if you see it please collect and recycle/do as you see fit, I hate the thought of having littered!!!!
Though partially closed, still a good hike with a great view.
Dirt road to the trail was ok.  Trail conditions were great imo
Trail is still closed at the lookout. Say hi to chippy.
Currently poste 8 to 12 are closed

This is my new favourite trail along hwy 60. It’s not as close to the highway as others - you’ll turn down Rock Lake road and proceed down a well maintained gravel road for 9 kms. You’ll enter a campground, and just keep driving. You’ll find the trailhead adjacent to a nice small beach on Rock Lake. As of Aug 2024, there is maintenance on the trail, and it’s closed at post 8. This turns it into a nearly 6km out and back instead of the 5+ loop. The closure is unfortunate as there are parts the I missed, but you do get to go as far as the lookout. This is the best lookout in the park, and even with some of the trail closed, it’s well worth it. The trail it self is clear and easy to navigate, and will likely be busy in the afternoon. Lots of roots, but it’s not different than any other Algonquin trail.
Half the trail was closed (turned into out and back) due to water damages
Great trails.  Haven’t don’t this trail in 19 years
Muddy and after point 8 the loop was closed, had to back track
The views at the lookout  are astounding. The trail is beautiful to hike.

This trail was partially closed for maintenance, but the open section is stunning. Having done many hikes in Algonquin Park, I can say this one offers my favourite view. Push through the forested sections, and you'll be rewarded with beautiful views of Rock Lake and the lush forest. Go out and enjoy this one!
Booths rock Algonquin Park . Great trail, but part of its closed down because the bridges out. So you climb to the top of the rock and then same trail back. Still well worth it.
Only got to do half of the loop cause it was washed out but, made it to the lookout! Great hike will come back when the full loop is open!
The trail is partially blocked, so you need to return shortly after the lookout. The trail was very muddy.
Very wet and muddy. Views are amazing from post 6-8.
Loop is closed, can do an out and back to marker 8. Worth walking through mud for the spectacular views

Very steep hike at one point somewhere in the middle of the trail. It was raining the night before so conditions were extremely muddy.
BUT the view was worth it! Finished in 2 hours
Lots of mud and mosquitos but nice looking trail. Got caught in a thunderstorm and didnt make it to the lookout
Half of trail was closed
Buggy

Beautiful hike but bugs were so bad. Use bug spray frequently and also recommend (if possible) coming on a more windy day. Also half the trail is closed so it’s currently an out and back rather than a loop.

Great trail
Lots of bugs but beautiful scenery and lookout
Few muddy parts but very doable. Quite a bit of mosquitoes however, so come prepared.
My husband and I and our dog sophie we hiked the trail today! U can't go past number 8 on the trail! It is closed from number 8 to 12! Beautiful lookouts!
Muddy in spots, but beautiful views and a nice easy ish hike
Rocky terrain with some steep sections! There’s a downed tree heading towards Gordon Lake! Very buggy and some muddy sections!
Trail closed at sign post 8, after lookouts.  Great hike, some mud, awesome view.
Closed between 8 and 12 so came up and went back down
a pretty steep hike, but no to difficult and well worth it!
Muddy in spots but great trail
A lot of mud, went there in March

Incredible trail with a bit
 of challenge. Not impressed with the other hikers who left a lot of personal kleenex and garbage on the trail including at the very top,  Love the views, not crowded, a little muddy. Also enjoyed the beaver  dam even though it made the last 500m of the trail quite muddy.

an easy trail. if you just want to find a good lookout without too much walk, you can just go to Algonquin Lookout Trail.  Much shorter and the lookout is better. 

is very muddy at the end if this trail.  ensure to have a good pair of shoes.
Do not come here after rain. The last rain was the day before yesterday. But the ground is still full of water and wet mud. It may destroy your shoesespecially near the exit.

The views are nice and the trail is well maintained; however, it's also incredibly busy during the fall. You don't generally go to Algonquin expecting jammed parking lots and crowds.
I think you can get views just as good at the Algonquin Lookout Trail or Centennial Ridges.

A little bit muddy. We did it clockwise, not very steep or challenging. But the rocks could be slippery in rain. Beautiful view at the lookout. There are wooden stairs while coming down so no difficulty at all. We completed in 2hrs 14mins with stops at the lookout.
I can't believe it's October. Feels more like a summer day with fall colours. Best of both worlds. Beautiful scenery and lookout. Not too many people on Trail itself but lookouts are busy.
Great trail. Not much mud today, path was clear.

Amazing trail, was not expecting to see so many mature hemlocks at the start of the trail. Forest got a bit younger afterwards but once again got older as it took us through mature groves of pine and hemlock. The view is spectacular. Hike down was easy with the many wooden stairs. Also great view points and small little beaches on the way back to the parking lot. Amazing fall hike. Personal favourite in Algonquin.
Not a lot of parking, but you can park further down the road. Make sure to buy the park pass ahead of time on their website as it gets sold out quickly.
The view is incredible. It's better to start the trail from the start point, so in the middle of the trail you will go downstairs not upstairs.
Probably my favorite lookout in the park.   Not a very difficult hike if you are average in your fitness.   Can get muddy/more difficult when it's wet but that goes for most trails.
Beautiful trail with lots of variety and views as good as Centennial Ridges.  New favourite trail in the park.
Great views

Trail was excellent. I've been quite immobile for 3 months, so I found this trail very strenuous. It was beautiful. Reaching the summit was amazing. Just to sit there in peace, as it was a Tuesday. It was a bit mucky, not a problem tho. The colours were amazing as I didn't expect this much change in September.
Trail in good condition.

Beautiful trail with multiple viewpoints. 
Interesting history. 
No bugs.
Great trail conditions, no mud!
Great lookout, only takes 2 hours
Probably the 8th time I've done this trail. My favorite in Algonquin!
Best trail

An excellent day hike for experiencing the varied ecosystems of Algonquin Provincial Park in a relatively short (6 km) time. The N to NE section has beautiful forest views and elevation to the lookout. Working your way south from the lookout is made easy with a winding set of stairs to the bottom. The south section is flat leading to the former grounds of the Barclay family (had a fun time trying to piece together the location of previously standing structures). The entire west side is flat and along Rock Lake, including a marsh view where an old mill used to operate.
Great trail. The climb up isn’t too bad and the lookout is worth every step.  Not too muddy and gorgeous views.
Great conditions currently on a wonderfully sunny day. No issues with bugs or mud. Get the guide before starting.
Not the easiest trail but well worth the view at the top :)
Fantastic views. Quite steep
Get good shoes. Last 500 meters of the hike very slushy.

Nice views…. Some narrow spots with the last 500M VERY muddy as it’s adjacent to a bog.
Some decent elevation and stairs to get down a portion of the way.
Good hike. Busy on the long weekend. Parking is small and we narrowly missed getting a ticket. Dog beach was good. Views were nice.

Fantastic trail. Very versatile with a mixed of covered forest, beautiful lookouts, and lakeside walk. The ascent is rewardingly challenging but the views from the top are well worth it. The last 500 m is extremely muddy. Highly recommend.
We’ll marked. Not hard. View from the rock is great. Definitely boggy on the return stretch by the lake.

Fantastic trail. There are not many bugs out, however, lots of roots and a little muddy due to the recent rain fall at the beginning at end of the trail, so wear some good boots!  The first half is an incline but worth the views at the top. Don't accidentally start at the exit as there's a section with only stairs that would be terrible to climb.
One of the best trails in the park in my opinion with views comparable to Centennial Ridges if you’re looking for a similar but shorter hike.

Great hike scenery and unbelievable view from the top. 
Took a dip in the lake on our way back..  lovely experience !
Fantastic views, varied terrain. Lots of rocky inclines and declines. Gets the heart rate up but totally worth it! I think it’s my favourite trail in Algonquin Park
Beautiful views. Fairly muddy with lots of roots to walk over. The first half is pretty steep, but worth it.
We loved exploring at Barclay's Estate make sure to hit that area.
Muddy near the end. Very well marked trail
We loved exploring at Barclay's Estate make sure to hit that area.

Steep inclined after post #5 most of it was slight inclined and ending was mostly flat terrain.  Very muddy for the last 500m towards parking lot.

Bugs were nearly nil during today’s hike, occasional mosquitoes during muddy areas but reasonable.

Amazing trail, very versatile with breathtaking views of the  endless greenery of Algonquin park and of the Rock lake. Muddy at times, but the worst part was the last 100 meters of the trail near beaver ponds, the trail was really muddy and flooded. It was possible to pass and keep your feet dry only wearing hiking boots. Nevertheless, the trail is definitely in my favorites list.

I went from counterclockwise (exit)
Aug 16 2023
Trail by the lake was flooded for 100m or more? If u have rain boots or waterproof shoes maybe no problem. But my shoes was soaked with mud. So I turnaround…
Very muddy between 11 and 12 but a beautiful lookout.
It has been raining  lots, so muddy throughout out.  Don't let the mud discourage you, tho, gh because you will miss spectacular scenery.
Muddy at the beginning of the trail and washed out along the bog due to the heavy rain two days ago. We wore waterproof hiking shoes and were fine. It's an easy trail for the view you get.
early morning hike.. very buggy. beautiful trail. lots of mushrooms! and an amazing view at booths rock
So many different mushrooms! First half was very buggy but got better after the lookout. Last bit of flat walking next to the bog was very wet after the recent rains.
Great but no wildlife
My husband and I hiked the trail  today with our dog  Sophie! It is a moderate trail to hike beautiful lookouts!

Some mosquitos but nothing that’s to be expected. Parking is limited - we were camping at rock lake so we walked to the trailhead from there. Following the trail in the recommended direction means you go down the stairs rather than up which I definitely prefer.

The first section of the trail is a lot of mud, mosquitos, and uphill. After that, the incline is nice and gradual. Lots of lookout points at the top, really beautiful view. If you take the optional trail down to the estate, you can sit by the water. After that, the walk back is flat trails along the water.
Very nice views but lots of mud.
Some muddy sections, but week worth the views
Amazing walk.  Beautiful view and cool lake path too.  Three different vista spots.

Trail was fairly easy. Took about 1hr and 45 minutes to complete, just forgot to stop the timer… however, it was a bit muddy due to the recent rainfall, but overall great hike with breathtaking views at the top

Muddy in the beginning, but gets better quickly. The climb to the lookouts is quite intense (prepare to sweat), but SO worth it! The views are breathtaking. Don’t stop at the first lookout - keep going, it get‘s better! The scenery is very versatile. You get a lot of different things to see in a short distance hike. Make sure to explore all of Barclay Estate: in the backside you’ll find remainders of the old mansion. The walk by the water is great for recovering the legs before you get back into the car. Also sign the visitors register in the beginning :)
Very muddy in sections, some steep climbs but gorgeous views.

The views at the top were beautiful.  The trail was very muddy and wet, however, despite muddy shoes, we were able to dodge around the worst of it and keep our socks dry.  The front half is climbing up rocks and roots, the back half is climbing down wooden staircases. We finished the trail in about 90 min at an average walking pace, but we didn’t stop for too long at the top. Bring bug spray!
Well maintained, overall great trail.  A little steep at certain sections toward the lookout, but  well worth it!  Bug spray recommended as a few sections were quite marshy
Stunning view on a clear day. This can be quite a muddy trail on a wet day. Bring bug spray!
Very muddy currently- took the trail backwards and enjoyed the decline
lots of nice lookouts. better than the lookout trail nearby. well maintained and only a few rougher sections
Great views! First lookout is really nice but if you’re stopping for lunch, wait for the second or third lookout since fewer people stop there. Views are just as good if not better
Lovely trail, nice lookouts, not too hard even though some of it is uphill.
A little swampy in some spots but there are ways around it. Bugs were moderate near the beginning but mild after that. Beautiful views.

Lots of mosquitoes and what looked like black flies and because it’s been raining the trail is very muddy - it would be a much better trail if it was drier. The worst part of the mud and slippery trail was the first third of it, after that the trail dries up significantly and is much better.

Fairly muddy in the first half of the trail. Hike is easy, slow elevation gain and ends off with a flat walk along the lake back to the parking lot.
BE SURE TO BRING LOTS OF BUG SPRAY.
Very beautiful, lots of mosquitoes in June, lots of different sceneries

Initially the trail was quite muddy but it does have an alternative route to take. The trail is INFESTED with mosquitos so a bug repellent is a must if you’re coming. The cliff view is amazing however and it made it all worth it! Other than bugs/muddy spots , it’s overall a nice trail that has lots of shady areas as well.
Great trail with great viewpoints

Really nice trail.  As others have stated there are some muddy patches but nothing too bad provided you're wearing proper hiking boots.  Mosquitoes are out in full force but found it manageable with pants, long sleeves, and bug spray.  Hiked in the late afternoon which made the view from the lookout point very pretty.
The trail is beautiful, but because of a LOT of mosquitoes we couldn't really enjoy it...
Well marked trail with great view at the top. Wear proper hiking shoes as parts of the trail are really muddy and slippery.

May 24 weekend was a zoo. Muddy from long rainstorm on Fri/Sat; wait another week. Black flies not bad, thankfully. 

This trail boasts some gorgeous views atop the cliff, but falls short of spectacular otherwise.  A bunch of nice smelling but otherwise normal Algonquin forest and a couple of chances to hop onto portage routes to peer at pretty small lakes. 

Best hike ever? No. But all that said, good exercise and no regrets when you’re up in this gorgeous country. 

If you start at the trailhead, once you reach the cliff note that are there are even prettier spots beyond the first stopping point you see where the view opens up. 

You can look to the right of the official trailhead as well to start on the flat bike path beside Rock Lake and hit the views a bit faster, and go down the other way. 

Beautiful day, not 5 stars, but nice way to see a bit of the Park.
Well maintained trail and pretty easy to manoeuvre muddy patches.
My boyfriend and I and my dog we hiked the trail  today! Beautiful lookouts even better than centennial ridges! Beautiful day for a hike!
might be a favorite trail at Algonquin. Beautiful lookout, great views all the way through.
Parking was closed near trailhead. Parked near the campground parking. Not very difficult hike but nice views from the bluffs overlooking the lake
definitely do not attempt in winter if you’re not ready to have some sore hips LOL

One of my favourites along the Hwy 60 corridor. Have done it a couple times because the views are great. You can easily do it in a couple hours - I consider it a liter version of Centennial Ridges. There are trade offs, and Booth's Rock is much busier, but you can still get some of the great views at about half the length of the trail. Parking can get super busy if you aren't camping at Rock Lake, so expect having to park far and adding 1-2km to your hike just getting to the trailhead
Stunning fall view!
Great trail. Clearly marked, pretty busy for a weekday however. Great views for a short hike.
great lookout for fall foliage.
Really nice trail. Multiple lookout points with amazing views. Fall colours were in full effect so it made for a beautiful hike.
Moderately easy trail although should carefully about your steps, lots of roots and rocks. Enjoy the nice view.
Beautiful trail, scenery is best when fall colors is blooming. I did not record all periods of length.  It is about 5.8Km. ^^
Awesome trail, very busy and many photo ops. Saw a beaver going across the first lake and many squirrels and birds. Saw a yellow-dumped Warbler and many chickadees and nuthatches.
Great views! great hike!

Not the best that Algonquin has to offer, but has a few interesting features. 
Longest trail staircase I have ever seen, Barclay estate remains and various shore view points, and some interesting Rock Lake views along the overly long rail trail.
If all you want is the lookout, cut the chase and head straight at it counterclockwise.  The rest is not that interesting.
Pretty easy trail, moderately busy. Very pretty views

One of my top favourite trails in the park. The end of the trail can normally be wet and muddy. Today was the driest I have ever seen it. No mud at all. Great trail if you don’t have time for Centennial Ridges. Same type of view.
Shorter than expected.  The kms along the water are very flat. Nice views but I'll stick to Centennial Ridge - bigger effort & bigger rewards.
Everything was so green and the scenic views took our breath away. We loved the peacefulness and the opportunity to absorb all the the beauty that nature laid before us.

A lot of steep forest trail build up for a fantastic cliff view pay off. Doesn't seem to be much at all left of the Barclay Estate. a couple of small foundation remnants of small sheds, asphalt clearing where the tennis court was and the old dock were all we could find.
A great hike little effort for a really great Lookout.  Trail is in great shape quite dry in the area this year
Easy but beautiful hike! Great way to spend a morning.
Well maintained, great views.
One of the best hikes within the hwy 60 corridor! Love coming back here!

They should've called it mini Centennial ridges. It's kinda like that except way easier, and only 1 lookout instead of dozens. Great for the novice hiker that isn't brave enough to go the full Centennial, but I likely won't do it again. Still, offers a lot of great Canadian Shield views and a bit of challenge. Do it clockwise unless you want to go up the stairs of doom instead of down.

Nice scenic views.
FYI Lost cell signal on first half of hike. I did download maps prior to hiking but they were not accessible. The trail is easy to follow. Bring a paper trail guide with you if this gives you security.
Great trail! Perfect to get yourself moving without overdoing it. Clockwise is the jam

We did this yesterday. Go clockwise then the number map will be easy to follow. Also at the end are lots of stairs and if everyone went one way there would be more solitude. We saw a few people having lunch at the overlooks. When we returned to the parking area it was full and when we started only 4 vehicles.  Go early. Beautiful hike.

We loved this hike for its waterfront and stunning cliff views. We did it counter-clockwise, which we enjoyed. This means we walked the flats (old railway line) first, then ascended. The rock cliff lookout surface was slippery after it rained so we stayed well away from the edges. The old ruins extension of the trail is not a necessary stop as there was not much to see.  We didn’t mind the hike up the umpteen stairs. Watch where you step. There is the occasional tiny frog that appears on various sections of the trail. Bring a camera!
Great hike; gorgeous views to reward the workout. Kids managed well with it. There are ruins of an old estate at the end which are interesting to explore.
Perfect! One of the best.

Nice trail .Interesting mix of forest, lake side and cliff lookouts. There is a bit of incline to get to the views, which was nice — makes you work for it a little so it feels like a reward . Perfect spot for a picnic at the top. I would recommend doing the loop clockwise to avoid going up the long set of wooden stairs. Just long enough to be a moderate challenge for kids. Completed on Aug 19 with 8 and 9 yr olds. The dip in Rock Lake at the end made for a perfect refreshing finish after a bit of work and sweating!  Enjoy

Beautiful views, although a decent incline to get to view. We are beginner hikers and just took a couple extra stops along the way. There is a nice little spot/mini beach to stop and take a swim near the end of the trail. Overall a beautiful trail.
Fantastic view from top of an intimidating cliff! Can’t wait to come back in the fall. Didn’t start tracking for first 25-30 minutes
My boyfriend and I and my dog sophie we hiked the trail  today! 3 time hiking this trail beautiful! It is a moderate trail!
Very nice 2 1/2 hr hike.

Start from rock lake camp site 
Took me 40min Counterclockwise to the top. Next time go watch sunset from the top. It’s gonna be perfect spot !
Amazing.  The best view of any hiking trail we have done. Fantastic.  The beavers were so cute!
Best so far in Algonquin
Great trail! Saw two beavers near the end of the trail.
Great hike challenging but not over the top. Beautiful views!
Challenging but not destroying. Awesome view from the rock.
Great scenic trail. Lots to see. Beautiful walk

There is something for everyone on this trail. It had beautiful cliff views of Rock Lake, but on the second half of the trail you can access the lake itself in multiple places. There are a few steep inclines but the real challenge is the mud. There is lots of it but it’s manageable with proper footwear, hiking experience, and some creativity to get through it or around it. The last couple of kms is washed out right now (beaver dam) though, and there is no way to get around it. It was ankle deep in places and you just have to suck it up. I recommend bringing a change of footwear to keep in the car. Note that you can drive right to the trailhead where there is a small parking lot across from a dog beach. Also, there were only a few bugs. Even with the soakers, it was an excellent hike. Really glad I fit it in on my last morning at Pog Lake.

Fantastic view, really cool detour to the old Barclay estate but pretty mucky for the final stretch alongside the beaver bog area. Overall great trail, steep climb but totally doable for a prepared beginner.
Good boy
Great trail
go anticlockwise on the trail! a little muddy but easy enough hike and spectacular views
The trail is beautiful, I will say it’s quite mucky and wet in multiple areas. Make sure to bring your waterproof hikers and you’ll be good
Best trail I've ever done, has it all and then some. make sure to pickup the pamphlet and sign your name at the trail head! PS: Bring extra socks, it's VERY muddy!! :D
We were the only one's out today snowshoeing.  It was beautiful and so quiet.
Not too much snow.  I was able to drive down the 8km road to get here.  Nice view at top.  Lots of wooden stairs.
Good challenging trail with an unreal view - did it in winter and there were some slippery sections overall.
We really enjoyed this trail.  Beautiful at the lookout.  Will spend more time up there next time.  Not crowded but it may be because you have to park the car at the campground office.
Awesome trail! Fairly easy going, the views are amazing!
Trail was breathtaking, slightly muddy on the return so wear boots, but 10/10 would do again!

Last hiked it in 2016. Loved the trail till I fell down the backside of it and rolled over 2/3 of it end over end until coming to a full-stop just short of impaling myself.  Permanent ankle damage but it was quite muddy, and I was hiking alone. 
Thank god for strangers. Highly recommend.
Beautiful trail all around ! However, it was quite muddy and the last bit of the hike (probably around km 3) it is pretty steep!

Easy end of moderate trail with very little elevation and a couple of amazing views. The end section was a bit muddy but overall good. Also the the entrance is blocked at the campgrounds office which adds 1 km one way roughly 10-15 mins.

Before you plan this trip be aware you need to walk a little farther to get to the trail as the bridge that leads you to it is closed for cars!!

Absolutely LOVE this trail! It did have some pretty muddy spots throughout and the incline could be difficult for some with all the roots, mud and rocks but, if you are in no rush and take your time going up you won’t be sorry! The view is just breathtaking and my family and I could have sat and looked out over the lookout point for HOURS. It also has an old estate that you can visit and find where the home, tennis court, fireplace, etc of the Barclay family. This trail is just all around beautiful and has a little bit of everything for everyone! We had our 4.5 month old with us and he enjoyed every second on the trail with lots of smiles and laughs as we hiked and saw chipmunks or squirrels run in front of us!
No too much mud. Great views it is worth it
Awesome view. A bit too late for peak colours but still worth it! A bit muddy but I expected that :)
Pretty muddy conditions right now so just be prepared for that. Very well marked trail and definitely worth the view
Extremely muddy conditions towards the end (or beginning depending on which way you take the loop, but the end for most people) so come prepped with proper footwear

This will not be an easy hike for anyone who finds themselves easily winded or is less than sure-footed. It is absolutely worth the trouble - I still can't believe how beautiful the vista is at the top. But the trail has many obstacles, including large muddy patches in wet weather, slick rocks on an incline and exposed tree roots. Even for a fairly fit adult, the hike might require many pauses along the way. If you have a camera in hand, you'll at least have the opportunity to photograph inside the forest along the trail while you catch your breath. For those with an eye for such things, the woodland paths are beautiful in themselves.
Great trail!! Muddy at the very end but worth the views.

We did this hike October 06 and found it to be excellent. Many high beautiful vistas and great views along the lake on the return end of the hike. The small extra hike to the Judge’s cottage is an easy addition to the hike. Much easier hike than Tower and Track and with more vistas. Enjoy
Amazing views, few steep hills and a muddy way back but overall very nice trail!
awesome views from the top. lots of muck on the way, which is sometimes treacherous
Bit muddy but day was nice and clear. Moderate hike.

Great trail with sensational fall colour views right now. The hike was nice with uphill following a creek. A bit muddy at spots with all the rain but manageable. We did this in about 1hr 40min with some time at the lookout to enjoy the views.

One of the top hikes in Algonquin, though a bit off highway 60 so fills up a little later. Beautiful views over Rock Lake. The climb up is moderate (equivalent to about one of the climbs on Centennial) and is worth it for sure. Great lakeside views on the return too.
It was our 3rd attempt to hike this trail (2 times sent back because the parking lot was full)and it was with it . Not too difficult and an amazing view on top.
Nice trail and worth the effort to see the beautiful vista. Make sure to do it clockwise for a nice surprise coming back down.
My boyfriend and I and my dog sophie we hiked the trail today! It is a moderate trail lots of steep spots and rocks! It was beautiful day great day for pictures!
My wife and I absolutely loved this trail. It's our favorite. Little intense at times but definitely worth the view!
Not too difficult, went by quickly and a beautiful view from the top!
Easy hiking. Started before 9:00 so no traffic. Great views.
Awesome views! My fav so far... <3

Amazing hike!!! Absolutely loved the challenge of the trail and the view. Recommend going clockwise as saw on Google to avoid going up the stairs. Just start at the entrance sign and follow the arrow direction on the map. Lots of uphill at the beginning which is a challenge but leads to an amazing lookout which is absolutely gorgeous! Final stretch is mainly even which is nice. Loved the views throughout! A bit muddy as it was a rainy day. Took us 2 hours with a couple breaks. 
Would skip the barclay estate as there’s not much to look at there.
Beautiful lookouts, mildly challenging well marked and maintained trail.  Definitely a favourite trail of Algonquin trails
Great trail with rewarding lookouts. Not very difficult with some stairs up and down. I would come early as it was fairly busy
Beautiful hike, nice lookout, slightly challenging
Easy.  Then difficult then easy.  Great views. Some fishing on way out. Some nibbles, no luck.  :)

Great hike. Lots of different scenery to take in. Steep inclines to gorgeous lookouts at a few different locations to take photos and relax. Visit to an old homestead of early settlers near the end of the trail. Lots of swimming locations along Rock Lake near the end of the trail. My kids did this trail when they were 5 and 9 and tolerated very well. Enjoyable for hikers of all levels in my opinion. Would definitely recommend.
Love the mix of the flat trail leading to the lake where you can swim, and also up the hill to see the high viewpoint. Doable for families.
Beautiful trail with spectacular views
Spectacular. !!! Not that muddy. One of the best trails in the park.
Great trail, lots of different viewing points/sceneries
Very nice moderate trail with very steep inclines to the extremely nice views then lots of steps down to a nice walk back
A little muddy for us in early august but still my favourite trail, high elevation to start but worth it for the way down on the way back

This was a great trail with a beautiful view after what felt like a short climb. It had a little bit of everything: river, beaver lodge, lake views and a beautiful climb and vista,  My 8 and 5 year olds had no issue completing this.  The end of the trail is a very easy and flat walk by the lake. Start from the end if you want to go up by the stairs.

One of my favourite hikes to date!
Tricky part is over in the first half (uphill climb), second half is smooth sailing (flat walk next to the water). Perfectly marked trail. Beautiful views. Mostly a forest walk, shaded. Muddy in spots BUT ways to go around it most of the time. Spots for my pup to cool down along the way.

Relatively easy but uphill hike; lookouts are amazing! It may be easier to start the trail "backwards" as you'll first get to a set of stairs that will take you to most of the lookouts, as opposed to starting at the beginning where you'll have to hike through a relatively buggy forest.
great view, otherwise a pleasant hike in the woods.

I completed it in 1hr 40 min and that includes chatting with strangers and meandering around the estate area. Very muddy at some points but a nice, challenging trail. If going uphill is tough for you, do it backwards and take the stairs to the lookout.
It’s worthy

Good trail, recommend it. Mostly forest with the usual rocks and roots, but also goes by some small lakes and marshes. First half has a lot of uphill but the views at the lookout points make it worth the climb. There were some pretty muddy spots but I had no problem navigating around them. My Garmin clocked about 5.5km and I finished in 1:40, including small breaks.

Very muddy trail so prepare ahead with good footwear. This took me about 1 h 11 mins (I’m mid 30a fairly fit; I did GPS and it’s about 4.94 km without going to the Barclay estate remains - cut this out as it started to storm badly). Trail is pretty easy to follow as blue markers well marked throughout. View point is a great spot to break or have a snack, or to Take photos. To get to parking lot from the road, turn in from rock lake campground sign off hwy 60 and follow the road down about 9km in to the trailhead. No bathrooms here so make sure to go when you see them on the way in.
trail was nice very muddy in parts as to be expected lookout was amazing great view of Rock Lake
So much mud, but the views are gorgeous!
Was muddy, but can avoid most of it if you get creative. Can be easy to slip when wet. Views are well worth it!

All in one trail. few amazing look out overlooking Rock lake. sharp cliff which is safe and breathtaking view. few snakes. Boardwalks and wooden staircase. Decent elevation throughout. Experience different types of vegetarian. Moderate and good for all levels of hikers. Took around 3Hrs. 
Be prepared for muddy trail.
Amazing view. Muddy trail but worth the mud. Good workout.
Awesome one of the best trails I’ve been on minus the mud at the end
Gorgeous hike, fairly quiet despite the busy campsites nearby. Please note the last leg of the trail has been overrun by a pond, and there is deep mud/water to walk through.

The climb up is challenging but worth the views! 2nd part is much easier but the trail is very wet near the end so would recommend wearing waterproof hikers. This is one of the best hikes in the park.
Amazing views. Fav Algonquin trail!
Such a gorgeous hike! 1km walk from the parking lot and $20 entrance fee totally worth it! Recommend going left to start and finishing beside the lake. Bring some snacks to enjoy at the look out
good hike with a couple of great viewpoints overlooking the lake. weren't too many bugs, even though it's the season (we may just have been lucky)!

My first hike at Algonquin park and it delivered as promised!! This trail has amazing views (possibly some of the best at Algonquin from what I heard) and it is very well marked. The majority of the hike was through a very green forest and had a fair amount of ups and downs. This takes you up to some cliffs from where the 180 degree views of the park are simply breathtaking. The last part is a calm walk along a gentle lake and then a bog. There are a few muddy sections overall, but I just did it in running shoes and it was fine. But the main downside of doing this trail at this time in May is the insane number of mosquitoes. Bring bug spray!! Also, the road through the campgrounds until the trail is closed currently. So you have to walk another extra 1km (each way) to get to the trail head
Amazing trail!! Beautiful view at the top, make sure to spend some time up there taking it in

the drive north was beautiful. was a great hike, at the end there was a long muddy patch unavoidable lol bought hiking books before next hike lol 
was awesome and can't wait to do it again.
Beautiful hike and lookouts.  Portion at the end near the beaver pond was flooded.  Note, parking lot closed, so add another 2.5 km round trip to get from gate to trail head and back.

great drive to algonquin, great hike, parts were abit difficult at times. Make sure you go clockwise if u want to avoid going up all them stairs. At the end of the hike we encountered about 10 min of a extreme muddy patch  but super fun.

Booth’s Rock Trail was lovely this time of year although the trails were quite wet and muddy so beware — dress appropriately! 

The trail started out with a beautiful walk through some of the nicest woodlands we’ve seen in the Park. It felt like it was straight out of a storybook.

While the trees have lost their leaves, the moss on the rocks and trees add a vibrancy to the forest that feels really special. There are also little bridges and staircases throughout the trail, which made for perfect photo opportunities.

The challenging part of the climb is condensed into a bit of a steep trek through the woods to the peak. However, once you get up there, you forget about any amount of energy you burned because it’s beautiful.

The lookout is amazing. There are plenty of places to stop and enjoy the scenery and take photos. We lucked out and had a snow flurry come in over the valley and hide the vista but then moments later, it cleared up again. The experience was magical.

One piece of advice for the cliffs: they are serious and there isn’t much separation between you and a far fall so keep your kiddos close and be careful. 

Highly recommend also adding the little walk out to Barclay Estate as well. It’s really neat to see the old foundation and there’s a little path down to the lake and two old stone docks.

The last leg of the trail was very, very wet and could be impassable without proper footwear. Highly recommend dressing accordingly! Rubber boots/waterproof hikers recommended.

Enjoy!

This trail is amazing and is marked really well! The view from the lookout is breathtaking and honestly makes walking through the flooded muddy area worth it! The mud in the beginning of the trail is bearable but beware that the last bit of the trail is extremely muddy and flooded... there is no way around it so make the best walking through it! Highly recommend this hike with appropriate shoes!

Beautiful trail! The lookouts were amazing and the trail was the perfect level of difficulty. Fair warning though the end of the trail is EXTREMELY muddy and wet right now (see photo). You can’t get around the mud/water either so be prepared to get your feet wet.
best hiking route we've done in Algonquin so far in 2020
Great

Awesome trail! Views were STUNNING. It was pretty mucky in places, but easily avoidable until the trail along on the lake at the end.. Highly recommend waterproof, non-slip boots if you're going this time of year. Rocks can be slick in some areas. Not a very difficult hike, but no walk in the park either. The lookout at the top was breathtaking! I imagine it's even more beautiful when the maples are turning.
Amazing trail worth the hill for view but stinky mud at the end sucks so bad!!!!
Beautiful view but muddy
Yes, it was mud through whole trail but it worse to go through and enjoy gorgeous lookout! Great trail, well marked.

It was a nice trail which will take you up to a cliff by a river and then you can come down through a beautiful path. A nice loop, I will say moderately difficult because of lots of puddles, stairs, and uneven terrain. But overall a nice experience.
The
Amazing trail with beautiful views of fall colors..!!!
Great lookout during fall colours. Well maintained and well marked. Follow the blue dots up the trail to the lookout and don’t forget to explore the old Baron’s homestead

Did the full trail returning via the lake this past Friday afternoon. Parking lot was emptying out when we arrived at 4. Seems a number of people heard about mud at end of trail and were returning back through the woods. In short, the mud is no problem unless you're wearing fashion trainers, it's at worst an inch or two deep and easily passable. Views from the top are amazing, and views lakeside just as beautiful (especially in fall). Be sure to do the whole thing!
nice trail. busy during covid nice weekends
Beautiful view of the lake from the peak. Trail also goes by the lake, boggy at the end.
Very beautiful fall colours. Recommend Taking the loop at left, the hill side first.. And returning from lake side .
Most of the trail was in great condition but a portion of the old railway section near Rock Lake was flooded by beavers at some point, and it is still quite muddy.
Best time of the season! Pretty muddy.  Parking lot full quickly.  Best red leafs view in Algonquine Park.
Great lookout. Followed the reports of the last couple of days and retraced our steps from the lookout.

A nice little hike with some great views. I went at 9:30 and there were only a few people, but by noon the parking lot was full on a Wednesday in late September. The last bit is muddy but not impassable. My cream coloured dog had no issues. Bring a towel and rinse off your dog and your feet in the lake after the hike.

Gorgeous views and not too demanding of a hike.  Elevation gain is mostly gradual in one long stretch maybe 15 minutes from the start.  There is a long and persistently muddy stretch along a pond near the end.  The views are just as nice as Centennial Ridges in my opinion, with a much less strenuous hike.

Spectacular views at the look out, easy to moderately easy hike. Like the previous hiker - the last km or so is completely flooded over from the bog beside it... the thickest mud, puddles and everything in between. A super pleasant hike up until that point but wish I read  up on conditions or that they were marked somewhere! Luckily I had extra socks and shoes
last part of trail needs repair. .way to wet and muddy

Beautiful hike! The first half is a little difficult hiking to the lookout but not too steep. The lookout is worth it! You can literally fall to your death here so be careful with kids and dogs! The 2nd half features stairs taking you down through beautiful forest. The last part on the abandoned railway is completely flooded for 1km. No way to stay dry. It’s knee deep mud and running water (1 star removed due to lack of warning for this). I would return the same way you came after exploring the lookout or you will be sorry.
Fabulous trail, difficult inclines but rewarding views! Entire last 1km is flooded, definitely wear proper shoes/boots!
Easy trail with a nice lookout at the halfway mark. Would recommend.
Great hike. A bit wet at the end as the trail was flooded.
Great trail with some amazing views.
Great trail with amazing point views to the Rock Lake! Totally worth it!
Trail has great scenes of Algonquin park. It was great experience however please do not go during rain as the last 300 meter became to muddy.

Amazing trail. One of my favorite along the 60 corridor. I've done it a few times over the years and both times the final stretch was underwater, so be prepared for some wading. but totally worth it for the views!
Great trail, bug free in September and incredible views that just kept on coming!
Hiked this trail after 24 hrs of rain. Best walk ever. From the random streams going through the path and the mist hanging low it was magical. Oh and that cliff is pretty cool too.
Great trail! Fairytale like forests with a beautiful look out. Saw some beavers in the last part of the trail.
Awesome hike. Very muddy in parts. FYI because we were surprised but you drive through the Rock Lake campground to access this hike.
Nice mix of elevation, scenery, lookout  and trees.

The trail was great, definitely worth going up hill (there were some steeper paths) for the amazing view at the lookout. For a novice hiker the path was considerably easy however it does get muddy after the rain and definitely slippery. Highly recommend to watch the sunset at the lookout but definitely bring a flashlight because it gets very dark.
Beauty trail

Beautiful trail!! Some decent hills to go up. Elevation increases quickly and it was a bit more challenging than expected. There are several bluffs with awesome views... keep going up higher for the best views! 
We were surprised how busy the parking lot was here, I think because of the beach. Loved finding a quiet little piece of beach all to ourselves near the end of the trail!
did this trail twice this year well maintained excellent hike.
Busy spot but great trail! No bugs today! Dog and I both loved the trail!
This trail is 5.1km long and fairly rigorous, rocks and tree roots as well as some steep inclines and descents. The trail runs along a cliff edge with a beautiful lookout and two small lakes.
Fantastic rugged trail with spectacular views! Highly recommend.
Nice and easy hike - offers a few excellent lookouts from cliffs. Can be a bit a bit messy after rain.

The view was beautiful!! Would love to go back in the fall. Rated moderate but found it more of an easy trail. The start was slightly muddy, and the final little stretch was practically all mud. Took about 2 hours to complete.

Very nice 3 lookout spots half way. The last 2kms on the trail is flat. The last 300m after the bridge was super muddy one day after a rain. Some people even turned around and redid 95% of the trail again to avoid mud. So if it rained recently you might want to do this trail backwards or be prepared to turn back just before the very end. We completed the trail in 2 hrs. The parking lot is too small and was full on a summer weekday. You also need to drive ~10km on a very bumpy dirt road (max speed 40) from highway to reach parking lot.

The favourite trail of all we did while we were in Algonquin. Not too long, not too short, and a little bit of everything (lookouts, woods, beach)! Can pass on doing the extra walk out to the remains of the estate- nothing to see there.
This trail has amazing scenic lookouts. stunning hike, not difficult.
I did this trail two years ago with my boys  and they had fun, they loved it and will do it again. We did this trail after biking for 13 KM and it was not too difficult. Go hiking...
Beautiful hike & incredible views!
One of my favourite trails I’ve done in Algonquin.
one of the best lookouts in Algonquin park so far
Well maintained, great views!

Trail was very clearly marked and easy to navigate. Took a little over two hours at a moderate pace with a few short stops along the way.  The views are absolutely worth the hike,  definitely take a camera with you! There are many stairs towards the end of this hike. My dog (beagle mix) had a great time navigating the trail with me.

July 2019- The home was easy at times and a little more challenging in the uphill areas. The trail itself was easy to navigate and well maintained. The lookout mid way definitely gives you satisfaction to have made it and motivation to finish. Also a beautiful view if you want to stop and have lunch/picnic. The lake near the end has a little beach which is great to cool off and end off the hike. 
Completed in 2 hrs including taking lots of time to take picture and have lunch.

Wonderful trail! Nice woody hike through a beautiful pine forest, then uphill to a gorgeous lookout with some great spots to rest and take in the scenery. Then down to a relaxing flat hike back along the water's edge. Not as crowded as Centennial Ridges (or as muddy or buggy).

This trail has some breathtaking views! The bugs were not too bad when we walked it and it was worth it when you made it up to the cliffs! In some areas it was a bit muddy but it had rained the day before so it was to be expected.

Had a lot of fun hiking this trail. My boyfriend and I completed this within an hour and a half with our dog. Views are beautiful and the hike itself was just fun. A little muddy but we found our way around it. Awesome hike! Bring water and bug spray, if you have bug spray for your dog it definitely helped. Would definitely recommend.

We have walked this trail within 2 hours... due to rain. However its a beautiful trail and after the climb you arrive at a beautiful overview. Even during the rain is was an amazing view. The way down is easy because of stairs. 

Bring mosquitospray!
Excellent trail with moderate elevation and beautiful lookouts. A great hike from start to finish.

This is Algonquin Park so the views are always good. Hiked this trail doing a amateur radio SOTA event. So we were carrying a bit of extra weight. 
The Trail was fairly muddy, but passable. The railroad section was a modest swamp. Ankle deep mud for 100m. 
I think a Moderate rating is a bit low but I understand that it is a short hike. The inbound climb is hard. It is only tough going up the one side. Going down there are stairs.   Bring a snack and sit for a while.
It was cold <8c so there were only 3 bugs, and I killed two of them.
Nice trail with amazing views!
we hiked this trail back in June.   great experience. bring lots of bug spray
Breathtaking views
Great views!

This hike was so great! So much to explore! Once you reach the lookout points the views keep getting better (3 lookout points, 6,7 &8) so check them all out before dedicating all your time to the first one!

This is my favourite trail. I just absolutely love the variety on the trail.  Amazing views lots of cardio in sections.  This trail is again not suitable as a stroll around the lake in FlipFlops. 
Pack lots of water. 
Picture taking opportunities everywhere.

Beautiful interpretive trail. Be sure to stop at each sign and read the description from the guide book. Copies can be purchased in advance or picked up at the trail head. There are multiple places to stop and eat lunch with a view at the top. Don't just stop at the first viewpoint. The side trip to see where the old estate was is worth the few extra minutes.
can't believe I did this
Awesome views, great trail for all...
Beautiful views at the lookout at the top of the rock!  Great variety in the trail terrain.
great view at the top looking over the lake given that you can find a spot amongst other hikers.

Great view of the lake from the lookout especially in the evening. There are a lot of stairs to walk down after the look out point, which ok but I rather be on the ground. For that reason I only give it 4 stars.
Excellent trail with amazing look-outs. Trail can be busy during the fall.
Nice trail!
Forest walk, rising steadily to cliff top view points. returning via a steep section of wooden stairs. Old railway section can be very wet and boggy.

Amazing view of Rock Lake. Very beautiful with fall colors. A little beach at the end.
Not too many mosquitoes in September compared with some other trails (for example Mizzy Lake!).
Easily accessible hike.
Amazing views of Rock Lake.
We had an awesome time on this trail! Brought our 20 month old daughter with us in the hiking backpack! Incredible lookout :)

Awesome views atop Rock Lake. Took my 10 year old son and myself just over two hours. Be prepared however. In June the mosquitoes inside the trail can be treacherous. Wear bug spray and bug net and you'll be fine. Worth the hike
A must-do Trail in Algonquin with gorgeous elevated views of Rock Lake. The only downside is that it can get quite crowded on long spring and summer weekends.
Amazing trail, definitly to put in your list if you are in the Algonquin parc. The views are breathtaking with many places to stop to rest while enjoying the sight. The stairs are pretty cool also.
Great trail, even in the rain. Fantastic views of autumn colours and plenty of quirky mushrooms to see in the forest.
Worth it for sure! The stairs are super cool and the view of rock lake is fantastic!

This trail has it all. It has An amazing lookout (in our opinion one of the best in Algonquin). The way up is not so terrible, but it is a good workout so you need to be in relatively good shape (for example no major knee problems..). The way back is really nice and smooth, in a path along the lake. It took us less than two hours. Definitely recommend it!! We did track and tower afterwards and in comparison we liked booth's rock better.

Booth's Rock Trail is a 5.1 km loop trail that visits two lakes and a spectacular lookout, returning via an abandoned railway. You will find ruins of Booth Rock, the railway he built. You will need to be prepared to do some climbing, but its not a hard job to do

In order to update my hike I had to use a previously recorded trail by somebody to sync up. The overview states primarily used for snowshoeing. I find this to be an odd statement as I've hiked this trail many times since a child with my parents in the summer and there has always been many cars in the parking lot.

Booth's Rock is a trail in Algonquin Park that starts at Rock Lake. The trail has a definite path that has both rock, and root throughout. Both are excellent natural staircases to use as you climb to the peaks for a great look at the surroundings.
